FOOD POISONING
Introduction
A spectrum of disorders arising from:
Ingestion of food and water contaminated by micro-organisms, and/or their
toxins, or by chemicals from non-infectious sources.
Clinical forms:
- Staphylococcal food poisoning:
- Food is contaminated by Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) when
prepared unhygienically by individuals who are carriers
- Subsequent growth of S. aureus in the food and enterotoxin production
occurs if the food is not cooked at temperatures sufficient to kill the
bacteria, or is not refrigerated
- Food-borne botulism
- Non-typhoidal Salmonellosis
- Shigellosis
- E. coli food poisoning
- Campylobacter food poisoning
- Listeria monocytogenes food poisoning
- Yersinia enterocolitica food poisoning
- Norwalk (Norovirus) virus food poisoning
- Hepatitis A virus food poisoning
- Giardiasis
- Helminthic parasitic food poisoning
- Others: Bacillus cereus, Vibrio cholera
